newsitem.title: MEXICO: Teck unit exploring Mexico gold sites.
newsitem.headline: Teck unit exploring Mexico gold sites.

text.p: The Mexican mining firm Minera Teck, a subsidiary of Canada's Teck Corp, invested $28 million from 1993 to 1996 on 26 exploration projects, a company official said Wednesday.
So far the explorations have yet to turn up a definitive site to mine but there are several encouraging leads, he said.
"(From 1993 to 1996) Minera Teck has invested more than $28 million on its exploration projects in Mexico," Roger Scammell, regional director for exploration, told Reuters.
"Once we find a mine, we'll exploit it, but we have to find it first," Scammell said.
Once a site is found, Minera Teck will form a new company for excavation, he said.
Among the promising projects is a possible gold deposit at Nukay in Guerrero state. Teck would work with Miranda Mining Development Corp on the project, he said.
At least 40 percent of the $28 million in exploration has gone to the Nukay project, Scammell said. Additional viability studies will be conducted in 1997, he said.
